intro: SYNC Manufacturing provides custom thermoplastic injection molding services for OEMs requiring precision, consistency, and dependable manufacturing performance.

blocks.text: Thermoplastic injection molding is a manufacturing process used to produce precision plastic components by injecting heated, molten material into a mold cavity.

Once the material fills the mold, it cools and solidifies into the desired shape. The mold opens, and the finished component is ejected. The process then repeats, allowing manufacturers to produce consistent parts efficiently across a wide range of production volumes.
Unlike thermoset materials, which undergo a permanent chemical curing reaction, thermoplastics can generally be reheated and remelted.
This makes thermoplastic injection molding a versatile manufacturing process for components requiring complex geometry, tight dimensional control, and repeatable performance.

Precision Injection Molding
We manufacture custom thermoplastic components ranging from simple industrial parts to complex geometries with demanding dimensional requirements.

Engineered Plastic Components
SYNC processes engineered thermoplastics selected for their mechanical, thermal, electrical, chemical, and dimensional performance.
These materials are used in applications where conventional commodity plastics may not provide the required performance characteristics.
Insert Molding
Insert molding allows metal or other compatible components to be incorporated directly into a molded plastic part.
Common applications include threaded inserts, electrical contacts, structural reinforcement, and mechanical assemblies.
By integrating multiple materials during molding, manufacturers can reduce downstream assembly requirements and create robust finished components.
Overmolding
Overmolding combines compatible materials or molded components into an integrated part.
Depending on material selection and product design, this process can provide improved grip, impact protection, sealing, insulation, or product functionality.
Our engineering team can evaluate overmolding opportunities based on component requirements, material compatibility, and available manufacturing processes.
Low- to High-Volume Production
SYNC supports a variety of manufacturing programs, from specialized lower-volume components to recurring production requirements.
We work with customers to identify suitable tooling, material, and production strategies based on anticipated demand and long-term program needs.
Material selection plays a critical role in determining component performance, manufacturability, and long-term reliability.
SYNC works with a wide range of thermoplastic resins, including commodity materials and high-performance engineering polymers.
Common Engineering Thermoplastics
ABS (Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene)
A versatile engineering thermoplastic offering impact resistance, rigidity, and good surface finish for industrial housings, covers, and structural components.
Polycarbonate (PC)
Known for its toughness, dimensional stability, and impact resistance. Commonly used in protective components, enclosures, and demanding industrial applications.
Acetal (POM / Delrin)
An engineering plastic offering low friction, wear resistance, and excellent dimensional characteristics for mechanical components, bushings, gears, and precision parts.
Nylon (Polyamide / PA)
Offers strength, toughness, and wear resistance, with grades suitable for bearings, mechanical components, and industrial equipment.
Polypropylene (PP)
A lightweight thermoplastic offering chemical resistance and cost-effective performance for a variety of molded components.
High-Performance Thermoplastics
PEEK (Polyetheretherketone)
A high-performance polymer known for thermal stability, mechanical strength, and chemical resistance in demanding operating environments.
PEI (Polyetherimide / ULTEM)
An engineered thermoplastic offering high-temperature performance, dimensional stability, and electrical properties suitable for specialized applications.
PPS (Polyphenylene Sulfide / Ryton)
Offers excellent chemical resistance, thermal stability, and dimensional control for high-performance industrial and electrical applications.

faq.q: What is the difference between thermoplastic and thermoset molding?

a.text: Thermoplastic injection molding uses materials that soften when heated and solidify when cooled. Thermoset molding uses materials that permanently cure through a chemical reaction.
Both processes offer advantages depending on operating temperatures, mechanical requirements, chemical exposure, and part design.

a.text: Yes. Insert molding allows metal components and other compatible inserts to be integrated into molded plastic parts.

faq.q: Does SYNC design and manufacture injection molds?

faq.q: Can SYNC help select the right plastic material?

a.text: Yes. Our engineering team can review application conditions, dimensional requirements, mechanical loads, chemical exposure, operating temperatures, and cost objectives to help identify suitable material options.
